newsitem.title: Mexico: Third death as Mexican fire is finally put out.
newsitem.headline: Third death as Mexican fire is finally put out.

text.p: Firefighters on Wednesday finally snuffed out a blaze in three huge fuel tanks that exploded just outside Mexico City, but a third victim died in a hospital of his burns.

As more than 5,000 evacuees from the northern suburb of San Juan Ixhuatepec returned to their homes, Mexican opposition congressmen demanded the resignation of the head of the state oil monopoly, Pemex, owner of the installation where Monday's explosion took place.
Live television pictures early on Wednesday showed the blackened ruins of the three burnt-out gasoline tanks where more than 100,000 barrels of fuel went up in flames.

Legislators and local news media were especially angry because San Juan Ixhuatepec had suffered an oil industry disaster before. Twelve years ago a series of natural gas tanks blew up there, killing 511 people and destroying homes over a wide area.
Pemex has also had a string of other fatal disasters in recent years, including a 1992 gasoline leak that blew up whole streets and killed more than 200 people in Mexico's second city, Guadalajara.

Pemex Chairman Adrian Lajous "must leave Pemex," left-wing senator Felix Salgado Macedonio said. "It is not right that he is still being kept in that job; ineptitude, incompetence and corruption is rampant in Pemex," he said.

Lajous refused to resign and brushed off calls for the San Juan fuel tanks and other dangerous installations to be relocated outside populated areas, saying a move would mean using more tanker trucks and causing even greater hazards.

"If my resignation would serve to improve the operating efficiency of Pemex or would serve to improve the security of our installations, I would seriously consider that possibility. I don't believe it would. I will stay at the head of this company," Lajous told a news conference.
At least 16 people were injured in the disaster, which sent huge clouds of black smoke billowing three miles (five km) into the sky.
Pemex said a fireman and a Pemex worker died in a hospital of their burns on Tuesday. Another fireman died early on Wednesday.
The disaster struck when Pemex workers were repairing a valve in a tank containing 80,000 barrels of fuel at a storage facility, but the exact cause was not known, Lajous said on Tuesday.
